On Windows, MaiCord 0.5.x and 0.6.x install this update from Settings > Updates. If you're still on 0.4.0, follow the one-time manual steps in the [0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/releases/tag/v0.5.0). New to Linux? See [Install](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord#install).

### Highlights

- **MaiCord for Linux.** The same client now runs on Linux: x86-64, a Wayland desktop and Linux 6.1 or newer.
  - Install it with the one-line `install.sh`, an AppImage, a tarball, or the signed apt, dnf and pacman repositories. The `.deb`, `.rpm` and Arch packages are attached too, and Alpine and Void use the `-musl` builds. The commands are in the README.
  - It has the Windows client's features: chat, voice and video, the plugin, theme and effect catalog, notifications, a tray icon, saved accounts, security keys and screen reader support. Windows Hello, the Windows notification page and the echo and noise reduction switch exist on Windows only.
  - The installer and tarball installs, and the AppImage, update from Settings > Updates. Packages update through your package manager, and the musl AppImage through AppImageUpdate.
  - The program is 6.5 MB. The tarball is 5.3 MB and the AppImage 5.9 MB.
- **Plugins and effects on Linux.** Plugins load as `.so` files and effects carry GLSL, from the same source as the Windows files. A catalog plugin appears on Linux once its Linux build is published, and each new version has one.
- **Windows.** No Windows features change, and MaiCord.exe is still 6.49 MB. MaiCord now identifies as the current Discord desktop client.
- **For developers.** `maicord-plugin build --target linux` builds a plugin's `.so`, and `maicord-plugin effect build --glsl yes --dxbc-from` adds an effect's GLSL. See the SDK and effects guides.
